intro: Anti-AI populism stealing headlines from the algorithms themselves — that's the story this Monday. From voters rejecting datacenter projects across nine states to Google strong-arming schools into accepting its AI tools, today's roundup captures a growing tension between the AI industry's ambitions and the public's appetite for pushing back. We've also got Anthropic dropping $3.4 billion on gas turbines, Trump weighing in on AI safety, and a founder running his company with Lord of the Rings-themed AI agents — because of course someone is.

stories.title: Tracing the contested history of 'equality talk' from Euclid to modern politics
stories.summary: Teresa M Bejan traces how the language of equality moved from mathematics to political philosophy, arguing that its apparent simplicity masks deep disagreements about what equality means, and that understanding its historical deployment can clarify modern debates.
stories.opinion: A thoughtful reminder that foundational political concepts are far less settled than they appear — useful for anyone frustrated by how 'equality' can mean opposite things to different people.

stories.title: Google warns schools: block our AI tools and you may lose Google Search too
stories.summary: Google announced new AI tools for schools but warned that schools opting to block its AI features could also lose access to Google Search. Parents and teachers across the US are calling the move extortion, arguing it removes meaningful choice from educators.
stories.opinion: A heavy-handed move that risks a serious backlash — tying a near-essential utility to acceptance of controversial new tools is the kind of bundling that invites regulatory scrutiny.

stories.title: Overly strict AI policies may backfire by increasing employee resistance
stories.summary: Harvard Business Review argues that rigid AI oversight can increase employee resistance to adoption, and that leaders should instead build trust, invest in skill development, and grant more autonomy in how workers use AI tools.
stories.opinion: Sensible but unsurprising advice — the real challenge is calibrating oversight when the risks of unsupervised AI use are still poorly understood.

stories.title: Founder built a Duolingo alternative with Codex and runs his company with Lord of the Rings-themed AI agents
stories.summary: William Imoh built Mural, an AI language tutor, using Codex and GPT-Live after finding that a 1,000-day Duolingo streak didn't help him converse in Norwegian. He also runs his 25-person company with Grok Bots named after Lord of the Rings characters connected to tools like Linear, Notion, and Pipedrive.
stories.opinion: An entertaining case study, though the $3-$5 cost per 30-minute voice session highlights that real-time AI tutoring is still expensive compared to traditional apps.

stories.title: Anthropic spends $3.4B on natural gas turbines to power AI infrastructure
stories.summary: Anthropic is purchasing Caterpillar natural gas turbines capable of producing up to 1.7 gigawatts, acquired after equipment supplier OnePWR failed to secure financing. The move is unusual for Anthropic, which has historically preferred renting infrastructure. Analysts warn natural gas prices could more than triple by decade's end.
stories.opinion: A remarkable shift from Anthropic's asset-light strategy that underscores just how desperate the power situation is for AI companies — though locking in natural gas when prices may spike is a significant gamble.

stories.title: Trump downplays AI safety risks in 60 Minutes interview, reveals DOJ threatened an AI exec with jail
stories.summary: In a 60 Minutes interview, President Trump said AI safety risks are 'not nearly as real' as executives warn and revealed the DOJ threatened an unnamed AI company leader with jail time for allegedly 'doing something bad with AI.' He said he would work with Democrats on AI guardrails but opposes regulations that put the US behind China, and continued promoting 'super intelligence' over 'artificial intelligence' as terminology.
stories.opinion: The revelation that DOJ threatened an AI executive with jail is the buried lede here — it suggests enforcement actions are already happening behind the scenes, even as the president publicly dismisses safety concerns.

stories.title: Anti-AI populism emerges as a defining force in American politics after 2026 midterms
stories.summary: Garrison Lovely argues in The Guardian that anti-AI populism is a major new political force following the Democrats' 2026 midterm sweep. Voters rejected datacenter projects in over 30 localities across nine states, 23% of voters cited AI as crucial to their decision, and AI industry leaders have effectively cast themselves as villains through their own statements about job destruction and existential risk. Lovely predicts AI will be the defining fight of the 2028 presidential cycle.
stories.opinion: A compelling argument that AI leaders' own doom-and-disruption rhetoric has handed populists the narrative on a platter — the 2028 implications are worth watching closely.

stories.title: Medium launches TK, a writing app with built-in AI assistance
stories.summary: Medium launched TK, a writing app where users invoke AI by typing '@TK' for quick questions, notes retrieval, and editorial feedback matched to publication style guides. Addressing controversy around AI in publishing, Medium positions AI as amplifying human writing and offers transparency features letting authors explain how AI was used.
stories.opinion: A pragmatic middle ground in the AI-writing debate — the transparency mechanism is a smart move, though whether readers will actually check provenance notes remains to be seen.

stories.title: Disney and Adobe partner to build proprietary generative AI models for Disney properties
stories.summary: Disney and Adobe announced a multiyear partnership to develop 'artist-led' generative AI models trained on Disney's characters, environments, and visual styles. Announced at Adobe's MAX conference, the deal gives Disney early access to Adobe Firefly Foundry for use across theme parks, cruise lines, ESPN content, and production pipelines.
stories.opinion: A significant legitimization of generative AI in entertainment — Disney's involvement signals that major IP holders see custom AI models as a way to control rather than resist the technology.

stories.title: Automattic launches Spacefast, a platform for deploying vibe-coded apps
stories.summary: Automattic launched Spacefast, a platform for deploying vibe-coded websites and apps that provides infrastructure (databases, authentication, file uploads, analytics) while letting users choose their own AI coding agent. Created during a company hackathon, it differentiates from competitors like Lovable by leveraging Automattic's existing CDN, WordPress integration, and WooCommerce capabilities.
stories.opinion: A shrewd infrastructure play — rather than competing on AI coding itself, Automattic bets that the deployment and hosting layer is where lasting value accrues as vibe-coding tools commoditize.

stories.title: RIAA CEO discusses the music industry's fight against AI companies over copyright
stories.summary: In a Decoder podcast interview, RIAA CEO Mitch Glazier discussed how the music industry, artists, and ordinary people now find themselves aligned against AI companies over unauthorized training on copyrighted works. Topics included AI deepfake legal complexities, potential bans and their free expression implications, and challenges of AI detection if platforms like Spotify and YouTube don't cooperate.
stories.opinion: The full-circle irony of the RIAA — once the villain suing Napster users — now positioned as defender of creators against Big Tech makes for a genuinely interesting narrative shift.

Using Notion as a “brain” for Grok Bot has been an incredible productivity hack, and how I built my fleet.

tweet_headlines.author: coreyganim
tweet_headlines.headline: Corey Ganim claims he's making __over $1,000 per hour as an AI Concierge__ by auditing, optimizing, and automating client workflows into Claude skills.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
Miles is right.

AI Concierge is one of the best ways to make money as an AI consultant right now.

I'm making over $1,000 per hour as an AI Concierge (99% profit) following this super simple playbook:

1. I like to start with an AI Opportunity Assessment. I spend 60ish minutes interviewing the client to figure out where AI fits into their biz. This is the roadmap we follow during our Concierge engagement.

2. We then book 2 45-60min Zoom calls a month. The client shares their screen and I help them turn their manual processes into Claude skills.

3. I run a framework called AOA for each skill build. We start by Auditing the manual process. Then we Optimize by cutting the steps that shouldn't exist. Lastly, we Automate by turning the new clean process into a skill.

4. In between calls I communicate with clients async via Voxer (a free walkie talkie app). I promise them a 12-business hour response time. I typically reply in under an hour in an attempt to overdeliver.

5. The client gets access to a shared Notion database where I log everything we build/optimize together. Then one of my own Claude skills reads their database and sends them updates after each call on what we accomplished.

The Notion hub is huge for retention because it shows the client in plain English exactly what we accomplished on each call, exactly what was automated, time saved, etc.

I'm basically being paid to identify a client's bottlenecks, help them clean up the process, then turn them into Claude skills.

If you're proficient with Claude (or ChatGPT) then this is a business model you can make great money with at extremely high margins.

tweet_headlines.author: AISystems_hq
tweet_headlines.headline: The case for __running an open-source model on your own drive__: one file, no login, no price changes, and it answers the same way in five years.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
I am begging you, download an open source AI model and keep it on your own drive.

It's one file, about 7 to 20GB, and the smaller ones run on a 16GB laptop. No login, no monthly plan, and it still answers with the wifi off.

The paid tools you lean on can change a price, a model or the rules overnight. A file on your drive answers the same way in five years as it does today.

Install Ollama (free, open source), type ollama run gemma4:12b, and give it the jobs you'd never paste into a website: contracts, client notes, your own numbers.

Setup takes about 20 minutes, most of it the download.

You'll be glad it's there the day a login stops working.

tweet_headlines.author: PawelHuryn
tweet_headlines.headline: Pawel Huryn, a non-coder PM, runs __5–6 Claude Code agents in parallel for up to 24 hours__ using a flight-deck artifact to track decisions instead of babysitting the chat.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
As a PM, I run 5-6 Claude Code agents in parallel, some for 24+ hours.

My 5 principles (no coding required):

1. Use any surface you want
→ Terminal, VS Code, or Claude Desktop: Claude Code does the same work in each.
→ New to it? Start with Claude Desktop's Code tab, not the chat.

2. Delegate outcomes, not steps
→ Give the goal, the desired outcomes, and how you'll measure success.
→ Add guardrails: what agents can't do on their own.
→ Then trust them. Mine work 12, 18, or 24+ hours without my input.

3. Read a flight deck, not the chat
→ After 24 hours, a chat is full of questions and open decisions.
→ My agents keep an artifact: what's done, what's in flight, and what's next.
→ I make decisions right in it. Telegram pings me only when they're blocked.
→ My /flight-deck skill is free (GitHub): phuryn/product-engineering

4. Prototype to align, ship to learn
→ Artifacts are great for sharing an idea and building alignment.
→ But you can't track what users do in them. For that, ship the real thing.
→ With agents, you get the first real version in hours.

5. Don't learn the tool. Let it teach you
→ Installing a skill or connecting an app? Don't Google it. Ask in the chat.
→ That solves 99% of problems. Don't be afraid to make mistakes.

I explained all five, and more, in 12 minutes with Moe Ali on @ProductFaculty's Agent Zero.
